title: Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal Player Ratings: Rice Saves Gunners From Rare European Defeat
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayOct 21, 2026Arsenal secured a decent result in Munich. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesDeclan Rice scored the all-important equalizer for Arsenal as they drew 2–2 away at Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Injuries and forced omissions dominated the discourse early in proceedings at the Allianz Arena. Bayern fielded a sub-par side without the likes of Michael Olise, Joshua Kimmich and Jamal Musiala, while Bukayo Saka’s concerning injury saw him substituted after just 10 minutes.

The absence of some glitzy superstars initially dulled a heavyweight contest, but Saka’s replacement, Eberechi Eze, sparked the match into life with his pinpoint strike in the 25th minute—which was initially ruled out for offside before VAR intervention.

Bayern responded 10 minutes later, however, as Alphonso Davies, playing in an unfamiliar left wing role, coolly converted Harry Kane’s sublime through ball. The latter then completed the turnaround on the hour as he thrashed home a penalty against his former north London rivals.

However, Kane’s international teammate delivered the final meaningful act of the match, with Rice lashing a strike beyond Manuel Neuer at the end of a well-worked move to maintain Arsenal’s unbeaten start to their European campaign.

Kane made his presence felt. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesKane has considered morphing into an NFL kicker when he retires from soccer, but the Englishman was Bayern’s quarterback in Bavaria. He touched every blade of grass, dropping deep to find space before unleashing some outrageous long-range passes—most notably the assist for Davies, which was executed with the utmost precision.
Oh, and there was his customary goal, too.

Arsenal boasted their own floating playmaker, however, with Martin Ødegaard matching Kane’s passing pedigree. The Norwegian delivered a sumptuous lofted through ball for Eze’s opener and was a constant source of invention for the away side. Everything was fed through the captain, who knew exactly when to speed up the tempo.

Arsenal will be fretting over Saka. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesTuesday’s action was littered with casualties as the likes of Ousmane Dembélé, Dani Olmo and, most tragically, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered injuries, and Saka joined a growing list of unfortunate forwards in Germany.

Arsenal will be fearing the worst considering Saka fell to the turf without any contact from a Bayern player, clutching his upper leg and leaving the field in serious discomfort. It could prove a sizeable blow for the reigning Premier League champions.

This wasn’t the best night for Saka’s clubmate Jurriën Timber, either. The Dutchman wasn’t dreadful by any means, but Davies left him for dead as Bayern equalized, and he proceeded to concede the spot kick from which Kane scored. Even the most consistent defenders can be bamboozled by Bayern’s fearsome forwards.
Davies made Arsenal sweat.  / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Manuel Neuer—6.6: The 40-year-old still boasts remarkable cat-like reflexes, as evidenced by his stunning close-range save to deny Bruno Guimarães.
RB: Konrad Laimer—5.9: Caught cold as Eze opened the scoring and found life challenging up against the England international. Perhaps he’d mentally prepared for a battle with Noni Madueke instead.
CB: Dayot Upamecano—7.6: Defensively sound throughout. One powerful foray forward would have culminated in a goal had it not been for an excellent David Raya save.
CB: Kim Min-jae—6.2: Rarely worked during the first half and was then substituted at the break.
LB: Josip Stanišić—6.6: Kept Eze narrowly onside by sitting too deep, but generally coped well against Madueke as the minutes ticked away.
CM: Tom Bischof—7.1: Robust in the center of the pitch against an industrious Arsenal midfield. Impressive given he’s just 21 years old.
CM: Aleksandar Pavlović—7.2: Another youngster in Bayern’s midfield which caught the eye. Pavlović has that beautiful blend of tenacity and grace.
